chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Salim, from Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said:

I said to Abu Abd Allah عليه السلام: May I be your ransom, what do you say about a woman who is on a journey with men, among whom she has no relative by kinship, and there is no woman with them, then the woman dies—what is to be done with her?

He said: From her, only that which Allah has made subject to tayammum is to be washed, and she is not to be touched, nor is anything of her beauties that Allah has commanded to be covered to be uncovered.
So I said: Then how is that to be done with her? He said: The inner sides of her palms are washed, then her face is washed.

key_terms.التَّيَمُّمَ: dry ablution, used here to indicate a limited substitute procedure
key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel or journeying away from one's place
key_terms.بَطْنُ كَفَّيْهَا: the inner sides of her palms
key_terms.ذُو رَحِمٍ: a blood relative or unmarriageable kin
key_terms.مَحَاسِنِهَا: her bodily features or parts whose exposure is to be avoided
key_terms.يُغَسَّلُ: is to be washed ritually for the deceased

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman dies in travel among unrelated men with no female relative present to wash her body?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the legal ruling concerning the preparation of a deceased woman for burial when she dies while traveling among unrelated men and no woman or mahram is present. It emphasizes preserving her modesty by avoiding touch and uncovering, while limiting the washing procedure to what is necessary in such constrained circumstances.
